hints.content:
When both factors are whole numbers, then:

$\blueD{\text{factor}} \times \blueD{\text{factor}} = \maroonD{\text{multiple}}$

$\blueD5 \times \blueD3 = \maroonD{15}$

So,

- $\blueD5$ and $\blueD3$ are $\blueD{\text{factors}}$ of $\maroonD{15}$.
- $\maroonD{15}$ is a $\maroonD{\text{multiple}}$ of $\blueD5$ and $\blueD3$.

The true statements are:

- $\blueD5$ is a factor of $\maroonD{15}$.

- $\maroonD{15}$ is a multiple of $\blueD5$.
